There's been a lot of talk about limiting conflict for now, and I had an idea earlier today that I think would do that very well. Definitely better than "ban technology" which I can see several different points of failure for.

The idea is this: An action which is in response to another action has restricted scope based on the source action. To force de-escalation it could be required that the response have a scope less than or equal to the original action.

Scope is rather loosely defined as the scale of the action in terms of what it affects. Examples of scope would be: {personal, local[small/medium/large], regional[small/medium/large], global, universal}. Any action would be required to declare its scope in meta text, as well as any action it was in response to. If someone felt that an action was declared to be a smaller scope than it merits they could ping an arbiter to arbitrate, as well as if someone feels an action was in response to an action it does not mention.

If later on we want more conflict we could reverse this to force escalation instead, or just get rid of scope restrictions when we don't care either way (presumably scope restrictions would be an Age rule).
I could see this potentially spiral into being unable to do anything at all. So nay.

This is a restriction on responses, not new chains of events. If something isn't in response to anything it could be universal scope, but once someone else gets personal the conflict has to stay personal.

My idea

1) Let's define scope as area of effect + magnitude of the effect. Don't preset terms.

Players should be reasonable "I throw a nuke on this one mortal." Does not affect one mortal. It affects a few cities (area) with a deadly maiming shockwave (magnitude) & it affects the globe (area) with radiation poisoning (magnitude).

Some of what you said here is very good, but I take issue with some of it too. Here's a point-by-point:

Players should be reasonable "I throw a nuke on this one mortal." Does not affect one mortal. It affects a few cities (area) with a deadly maiming shockwave (magnitude) & it affects the globe (area) with radiation poisoning (magnitude).

If someone calls a nuke personal (note that those are example scopes, not something we have to go with), that would be an obvious time to call in the arbiters. I would personally call a nuke either local large or regional small.

I oppose including magnitude in scope, not only because of difficulty measuring but because as long as scope (I am using the actual definition) is controlled magnitude can be allowed to range freely.

2) An action can be twarthed, but not moved away from it's original intent.

I'm not a big fan of this idea.

Some of the coolest stories and events that have taken place all started with small actions.

Look at how the greeks viewed the trojan war, look at how world war 2 started, each started with relatively small actions.

One was throwing an apple into a wedding - a personal action, the other was an assassination of a political figure - a country-wide action, yet both spiralled out of control in incredible ways.

These sorts of restrictions can really kill some potentials for awesome storytelling. What people need to do instead is simply be more respectful towards each-other and what they are trying to do. It would be great if there was more conversation outside of the posts to discuss how people would like a story to progress and how each player can reach their intended goals with the conflict.
